predecessors.name: Duchy of Pomerania
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's Pomerania outline of 1187 (Bogislaw I died in 1187; the duchy 'a Danish vassal' after 1185)

successors.name: Swedish Empire
successors.text: 'At the Peace of Westphalia in 1648 and the Treaty of Stettin in 1653, Sweden received Western Pomerania' with Rügen, Usedom, Wollin and a strip east of the Oder with Damm and Gollnow

successors.name: Brandenburg-Prussia
successors.text: 'Brandenburg-Prussia received Farther Pomerania (Hinterpommern)': the part of the former duchy east of the Oder except Stettin

ledger.x: 13th century, tied to 1250: the Uckermark goes to Brandenburg.
1317: 'was extended by the Lands of Schlawe and Stolp in 1317.'

1325: Rügen. 'after the last Rugian prince Wizlaw III died in 1325' the principality passed to the Griffins (Wartislaw IV, 1325-1326, heads the list of rulers); the Duchy page dates the acquisition of 'the Principality of Rügen in 1325'. Two wars with Mecklenburg followed.
1341: Stolp redeemed from the Teutonic Order (end of the 1329-1341 pledge).

1478: Bogislaw X reunites the duchy (infobox 'Reunited under Bogislaw X: 1478'); it had been partitioned between Wolgast and Stettin in 1295 ('a partition ... that would last until 1464' on the page).
10 March 1637: the duchy ends with Bogislaw XIV's death; the Swedes stay in the land until the partition of 1648 (Swedish Pomerania page).

10 March 1637: 'Death of Duke Bogislaw XIV: 10 March 1637'; 'the duchy was partitioned between Brandenburg-Prussia and Sweden' (Peace of Westphalia 1648, Treaty of Stettin 1653 for Sweden; Farther Pomerania to Brandenburg-Prussia).

wars.name: Swedish occupation of Pomerania
wars.outcome: Gustavus Adolphus 'had occupied much of Pomerania on entering the Thirty Years' War in 1629' and the Swedes completed the occupation by the end of 1630 (Treaty of Stettin, 10 July 1630); the duchy ended in 1637 and was split at Westphalia.

certainty.note: The pages give lands and treaties, not boundaries; the outline is Cliopatria's 1187 shape with circles for the dated additions and losses.
As above; the Lauenburg and Bütow Land was a Polish fief from 1526.
